title: Finger Exercise 12 — count_sqrts
statement:
Implement `count_sqrts(nums_list)`.

- `nums_list`: a list. Assume it contains only positive numbers and has no duplicates.
- Return **how many elements** in `nums_list` are exact squares of elements in the same list (an element may be its own square, e.g. `1`).

```
count_sqrts([3, 4, 2, 1, 9, 25]) -> 3
```
Here `4 == 2*2`, `9 == 3*3`, and `1 == 1*1`, so three elements are squares of list members.

Source: MIT OCW 6.100L Fall 2022, Finger Exercise Lecture 12 (reconstructed as a runnable problem for this study tool).
